nuestras: nuestro — our (possessive fem. pl.; nuestras oraçiones 'our prayers'; = nuestras)
al: a + el — to the; al menos 'even the least' · also a + el standing for a + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (al espada = a la espada) · also al — 'other thing, the rest' (neuter, Latin alius; de lo al non pienssan nada 'of anything else they think nothing'; distinct from a + el) · also a + el before an infinitive 'on, upon' (al exir de Salón 'on leaving the Jalón'; = al salir) · al 'the other thing, the rest' in al feredes adelant 'the rest you will do later' · also por al 'otherwise, for any other reason' (non passará por al 'it will not be otherwise'); a mí mandedes al 'order me something else', give me another charge (the likelier reading of a terse line)
çid: Çid — the Cid, 'lord' (Arabic sīdī 'my lord'; pronounced Tsid)
campeador: Campeador — the Battler, the Champion (the Cid's epithet, from campo 'field of battle')
que: que — that, who, which; for · also por que — because, since (= porque) · por que — by which, whereby (por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more') · also que — 'so that, lest' introducing purpose/result (que por miedo non dexen nada; por tal lo faze … que no lo ventasse nadi); after después/mientra 'after, while' (después que, mientra que) · also que — than, after a comparative (mas le vienen … que nos le van 'more come to him than leave him') · also que — what (indirect interrogative; dezir vos he que faze 'I shall tell you what he does'; = qué)
las: el/la — the (fem. pl.); them (fem. object pronoun)
a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado) · personal a before a direct object (salvest a Jonás; a ti adoro); a + inf. 'to, about to' (tornólas a catar); a tan grand sabor 'with so great pleasure'; a ojo 'in plain sight' · also a — 'into' (sacar a çelada 'to lure into ambush'); 'at, in' (a la çaga 'at the rear'); 'against' (dar salto a la çaga); dative 'to' (a mí dedes); haber a + inf. 'have to' (lo han a far); a + noun of direction (adeliñava a la puerta 'made for the gate') · impersonal 'there is' (aver; es dia a de plazo 'there is (only) a day of the term', the most likely reading of a hard line); ha as auxiliary set after the participle (soñado a 'he has dreamt') · also 'on, at (a time)' (a tercer dia 'on the third day') · also a — 'has' before the participle, agreeing with the object (la lança a quebrada 'he has broken the lance'; a menester 'has need of'); a + dative of the person affected (a Minaya matáronle el cavallo 'they killed Minaya's horse') · a — 'as, for' (tóvoslo a grand fonta 'he took it as a great affront') · also a — 'with' of instrument (a dientes las tomó 'with his teeth he took them'; = con) · also prender a espolonada — 'to begin the attack, charge' (priso a espolonada, Pidal 'comenzó el ataque'); pendón a corças 'a banner with (a device of) roe-does' (a = 'with', likely)
tierras: tierra — land (pl.; = tierras) · also a tierras — 'to the ground' (a tierras firió 'he dismounted', Pidal 'echó pie a tierra'; = a tierra)
de: de — of, from · also de — by (the agent with a passive participle; = por) · also de — 'by (night)' (de noch), partitive 'of, among' (quinze moros … de los que alcançava; pocas de gentes), 'as' (de ganançia 'as booty'), 'from outside' (de fuera), 'on the right' (de diestro) · also 'about, concerning' (de mí non digan mal 'let them not speak ill of me') · also de — 'as if in' (commo de arrancada 'as if in rout'); 'in the manner of' (de guisa 'in such a way'); 'of, among' (de bivos pocos 'of the living few'); nominalized infinitive (del prender 'of the taking') · also de — 'with' of manner (de fuertes coraçones 'with stout hearts'); 'on' (de pie 'on foot'); 'from' of side (della e della part 'from both sides'); de cabo 'anew' (de + cabo, 'again'); de suso de 'above'; seños … de seños colpes 'with one blow each' · also de — 'in respect of' after an adjective (sobejana de mala 'exceedingly bad'); 'with regard to, about' (me plaze de mio Çid 'I am pleased about the Cid'); 'from, at the hand of' (de señor non ha graçia 'he gets no favor from a lord'); 'from' of origin (de moros fo 'it came from Moors'); 'at' of manner (de vagar 'at leisure', de + the noun vagar) · also de’ — Pidal's de’llaño, read as del llaño 'of the plain' (the article's l run into the ll; a reading, not certain) · de + infinitive after an adjective (de ir somos guisados 'we are ready to go') · also de + infinitive after a verb: començar de 'to begin to' (compeçó de fablar 'he began to speak'), piénssanse de 'set about' (piénssanse de armar), aver de 'to have to' (lo que ha de far 'what he has to do') · also de — 'within' of a time limit (De aquestos quinze días, most likely 'within these fifteen days'; sense uncertain); de veluntad 'willingly'; de + superlative partitive (de los mejores guarnimientos 'of the best equipment') · also de — 'with, from' of the means or source (diziendo de la boca 'saying with his mouth'; de cuer les pesa 'it grieves them from the heart') · also de que 'of whom, of which' (relative after a noun; de moros de que non avien sabor 'of Moors they had no taste for') · de firme 'steadfastly, with a will' (de firme robavan el campo); de + noun of material, 'in' (de plata seys çientos marcos 'six hundred marks in silver'); of possession, 'belonging to' (de vos son 'are yours'); fartos de lidiar 'sated with fighting'; pagado de 'pleased with'
carrión: Carrión — Carrión de los Condes, town in Palencia, seat of the counts of Carrión (= Carrión)
hemos: aver — we will/shall (1st pl. future auxiliary; restored by Pidal in the split future dar gelos [hemos] = se los daremos)
do: do — where, as (relative adverb, Latin de ubi; = donde) · also do — wherever, whenever (generalizing, with subjunctive: do yo vos enbiás 'wherever I might send you'; the exact sense is uncertain) · also dar — I give (present 1st sg.; d'aquí vos do mi graçia 'from here I give you my favor'; = doy) · also do — for don, 'lord' (title before a name; el obispo do Jero[me] 'the bishop don Jerome')
ellas: ella — they, them (fem. pl., stressed; con ellas 'with them'; = ellas)
son: seer — they are (3rd pl.) · also son — perfect auxiliary of intransitives and passive auxiliary (todos son exidos 'have all gone out'; nombrados son; son derramadas 'are scattered')
sacar: sacar — to take out, bring away (infinitive; dexe sacar 'let (me) take (them) out'; = sacar)
valençia: Valençia — Valencia, the Moorish kingdom and city whose king Tamín is addressed (= Valencia) · also Valençia — the city itself, held by the Cid (en Valençia sedí mio Çid 'in Valencia was my Cid'; Valençia vienen çercar 'they come to besiege Valencia')
poder: poder — to be able (infinitive; first half of a split future, poder nos han alcançar 'they will be able to overtake us'; = poder) · also poder — power, hands, control (noun; en so poder 'in his keeping'; = poder)
del: de + el — of the (contraction) · also del standing for de + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (del albergada = de la albergada) · also del — 'from, for, because of' (cause; del gozo 'from the joy'; del çerviçio 'for the service')
después: después — afterward, then · also después que — since, seeing that (causal; después que de moros fo 'since it came from Moors')
en: en — in, into, on · en — of it, thence (= ende; por en avemos qué fablar 'of which we have to speak') · also en — 'as' (en paria 'as tribute'); en essora 'at that moment' · also en — 'among' (en todos los sos 'among all his men') · also en + infinitive 'in (doing)' (en levarlo adelant 'in carrying it forward'); en çinco días 'in five days'
la: el/la — the (fem.); her/it (object pronoun) · also la que 'the one that' (Çelfa la que dizen de Canal 'Çelfa, the one they call of the Canal')
carrera: carrera — road, way, journey (en la carrera 'on the road'; = carrera, now mostly 'race, career')
feremos: fazer — we shall make, win (future 1st pl., syncopated; feremos ganançia 'we shall make gain'; = haremos) · also fazer — we shall do (feremos lo que ploguiere a vos 'we shall do what pleases you'; = haremos)
sabor: sabor — pleasure, wish; a so sabor 'at his (their) pleasure' · also por sabor de 'out of a wish to please, for the sake of' (por sabor de mio Çid 'to please the Cid') · also por sabor que — 'out of the desire (that)' (por sabor que avía de algún moro matare 'out of the longing I had to kill some Moor') · also aver sabor — to long for, to wish (lo que avía sabor 'what I longed for'; a qui yo ovier sabor 'to whomever I please', Pidal 'quisiere')
ante: ante — before; ante que 'before (that)' · also ante — because of, at (of the cause, like Latin prae; ante roído de atamores 'at the din of the drums')
nos: nos — we (subject pronoun; = nosotros) · also nos — us, to us (object pronoun; atorgar nos hedes 'you will grant us') · also reflexive 'ourselves' (nos partimos 'we part'); dative (la missa nos dirá 'will say for us') · also nos' — non + se (aun nos' van del campo 'they are still not leaving the field'; the apostrophe marks the elision) · also nos — non + se, written without apostrophe (nin amigo a amigo nos pueden consolar 'nor can friend console friend'; mas le vienen … que nos le van 'more come to him than leave him', the no redundant after the comparison)
lo: lo — him, it (object pronoun) · lo que perdedes 'that which you lose' (neuter antecedent of the relative) · also lo — neuter article 'what is' (lo to 'what is yours'); pleonastic 'it' (lo an, lo han a far; por tal lo faze 'for that reason he does it')
cuntió: cuntir — it happened, befell (preterite 3rd sg.; que les cuntió 'that befell them', Pidal 'les aconteció'; = aconteció)
león: León — León, the kingdom and city (Alfons el de León 'Alfonso of León'; = León) · also león — lion, the animal (masc.; saliós … el león 'the lion broke loose', adeliñó para' león 'he made straight for the lion'; = león), not the kingdom
natura: natura — birth, lineage (de grand natura 'of high birth'; = linaje, naturaleza)
somos: seer — we are (1st pl. of seer = ser)
comdes: conde — counts (pl., Pidal's co[m]des; de comdes de Carrión 'of the counts of Carrión'; = condes)
averes: aver — goods, possessions, wealth (aver as noun, pl.)
canpeador: Campeador — spelling variant with n for m (copyist's spelling) of Campeador, the Cid's epithet
d: de — of, with (elided form of de before a vowel, d'arena = de arena) · de — from (unos d'otros 'one from another') · also d — 'about, concerning' (D' iffantes de Carrión yo vos quiero contar 'of the Infantes of Carrión I wish to tell you'; = de)
aquestos: aqueste — these (masc. pl., 'aqueste' = este with prefixed aque-; aquestos dos reyes 'these two kings'; = estos)
seremos: seer — we shall be (future 1st pl.; = seremos)
podremos: poder — we shall be able (future 1st pl.; = podremos)
casar: casar — to marry off, to be married (infinitive; por casar son vuestras fijas 'your daughters are to be married'; por + inf. 'still to be done'; = casar) · also casar — to marry (infinitive, active, of the suitors; casar queremos con ellas 'we wish to marry them'; = casar)
con: con — with · also con — 'with the help of' (con Dios 'with God's help'; verlo hemos con Dios 'we shall see it with God's help')
o: o — or; also ó — where (interrogative, Latin ubi; ¿O sodes…? 'Where are you…?') · also o — where (relative adverb; o dizen Castejón 'which they call Castejón'; o el Campeador estava 'where the Campeador was'; = donde) · correlative 'either … or' (o me dexaredes … o … levaredes 'either you will leave me … or you will take away')
ca: ca — for, because (Latin quia) · ca — perhaps 'but, whereas' (el uno es en paradiso, ca el otro non entró allá; the sense is uncertain) · also ca non — 'and not that' (Pidal 'y no que'; cuédanse que es almofalla, ca non vienen con mandado 'they think it is an army, and not that they come with a message')
assí: assí — thus, so (= así) · also assí — so greatly, so much (Pidal 'de tal modo, mucho'; assí envergonçó 'was so abashed')
antes: antes — before; antes de 'before' · also antes que — 'before' (conjunction; antes quel prendan 'before they take him') · also antes — 'rather' (antes perderé el cuerpo 'rather shall I lose my body')
fo: seer (and ir, which shares this preterite) — he/it was; went (preterite 3rd sg.; = fue, restored by Pidal as f[o]; of this part's three occurrences, fo entrado and fo acusado are periphrastic/passive ser + past part. constructions, while fo algo is a plain copula with a pronoun predicate, 'was something') · also commo fo tu voluntad, ca fo tu voluntad 'as/for it was your will' (ser + noun subject, 'it was'; Pidal restores f[o]) · also se fo acomendar 'went to commend himself' (ir); fo de noch 'it was night' (ser de + noun, 'night had come'); fo desenparada (passive, 'was abandoned') · also fo — went (ir; mañanas fo Minaya 'in the morning Minaya went'); fo de moros 'it came from the Moors' (ser de + noun of origin; Pidal restores f[o]) · also fo — it was, ser + adjective predicate (Buena fo la de Valençia 'good was the (capture) of Valencia'; Pidal restores f[o])
conssejo: conssejo — help, remedy (spelling variant of consejo; Pidal 'amparo, socorro'; = consejo) · also conssejo — council, deliberation (fablando en so conssejo 'talking in their council'; = consejo) · also conssejo — counsel, advice (con vuestro conssejo 'with your counsel'; = consejo)
tornados: tornar — turned back, returned (past part. masc. pl., agreeing with los 'them'; a los moros dentro los an tornados 'they have put the Moors back inside'; = vueltos, devueltos) · also tornar — turned back, returned (intransitive, with ser; tornados son 'they have turned back'; = vueltos)
fabló: fablar — he spoke (preterite; = habló, note f-)
ferrant: Ferrant — Fernando (personal name; Pidal's Ferran[t]; Ferrant Gonçalvez, one of the two Infantes of Carrión; = Fernando)
gonçálvez: Gonçálvez — González, patronymic 'son of Gonçalo' (Gonçál[v]ez, the v supplied; here Asur González; = González)
e: e — and (= modern y) · also aver — I have (1st sg. present, apocopated form of he, perfect auxiliary: Espeso e el oro, 'I have spent the gold') · also aver — 'I will', the future auxiliary in a split future (quitarvos e … darvos e de mano 'I will free you … I will let you go'; = vos quitaré, vos daré) · also the full verb 'I have' (el sabor que dend e 'the delight I have of it') · also e — pleonastic 'and' joining two names of the one person (a Dios e al padre 'to God, the Father'; Pidal 'conjunción e pleonástica', cf. v. 300)
fizo: fazer — he made, did, caused (strong preterite 3rd sg.; fizo posar 'he made (them) halt'; = hizo)
cort: cort — court, royal or lordly household (fem. noun; en mi cort 'in my court'; = corte)
sí: sí — so, thus (optative particle, Latin sic; sí el Criador vos salue 'so may the Creator save you'; = así, no modern use as a particle) · also sí — himself, oneself (reflexive pronoun after a preposition; cada uno por sí 'each on his own account')
vos: vos — you (object pronoun, polite/plural) · also subject 'you' (vos, que por mí dexades 'you who leave for my sake'); dative 'to you' (dar vos quiero vuestra part) · also reflexive/ethic 'you (yourselves)' (id vos en algara 'go off on a raid'); dative with an impersonal sense (si cueta vos fore 'if need befall you')
vala: valer — may he avail, protect (present subjunctive; vos vala 'may he keep you')
el: el — the (masc.) · also el — 'he who' before a relative (el qui quisiere, el que es sobre Fenares); el before a fem. noun beginning with a vowel (el espada = la espada; el algara = la algara) · also el de + place name 'he of, the one from' (mio Çid el de Bivar)
plega: plazer — may it please (present subjunctive 3rd sg.; plega a Dios 'may it please God'; = plazca)
doña: doña — lady (title; Latin domina, fem. of don)
minaya: Minaya — the title by which the Cid's kinsman Álvar Fáñez is called, usually explained as mi + anaya 'my brother'
álbar: Álbar — Álvar (personal name, Álbar Fáñez; = Álvar)
quantos: quanto — as many as (masc. pl.; todos quantos 'all who'; = cuantos)
aquí: aquí — here; d'aquí 'from here' · also 'then, at this point' (aquí dixo el comde 'then the count said')
dadnos: dar + nos — give us! (imperative 2nd pl. dad + enclitic nos; = dadnos)
avemos: aver — we have (present 1st pl.; = hemos) · avemos de + inf. 'we must' (mucho avemos de andar 'we have far to go'); avemos qué fablar 'we have something to speak of' · also perfect auxiliary aver + participle (avemos preso 'we have taken')
bendiçiones: bendiçión — blessing (fem. pl.; prendan bendiçiones 'let them receive blessings'; = bendiciones)
levar: levar — to carry, carry off (= llevar)
meter: meter — to put, set (infinitive; vo meter la vuestra seña 'I go to put your banner'; = meter)
les: les — to them · also les — 'from them', dative of removal or injury (les tollió el pan 'took the bread from them'; viédales exir 'forbids them to go out')
por: por — through, along, by, for · purpose, 'in order to' (por el reyno quitar 'to quit the kingdom'); por + inf. 'yet to be done' (tres an por troçir 'three remain to pass'); 'for, on behalf of' (por mio Çid) · also por — 'out of, because of' (por miedo 'through fear'); 'for (that reason)' (por tal lo faze 'he does it for that reason'); 'by way of' (por Guadalfajara); por + noun 'for the sake of' ; por coraçón 'willingly' · also 'for (a price)' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'by means of' (por carta 'by writ'); 'through, thanks to' (por mí ganaredes 'through me you will gain') · also por — 'on, during (a time)' (por aquesta mañana 'this morning'); 'by way of, through' (por medio de la llaña 'through the middle of the plain') · also por — 'in' after fiar (yo fío por Dios 'I trust in God') · also por — 'to fetch, for' after enbiar/ir (enbiaré por ellas, irán por ellas 'I shall send for them', 'they will go for them'); por cuenta 'by count, in a count' · also por — as (por heredad 'as a possession') · also por — 'about, after' with preguntar (por el rey tómanse a preguntar 'they begin to ask after the king'); por + infinitive 'for … to' (por … vençer reyes, 'for … to defeat kings')
onores: onor — estate, landed property, honor (pl.; = honores)
los: el — the (masc. pl.); them (object pronoun) · also los que 'those who' (demonstrative use before a relative); los — him, them as object of consejar (commo los consejava 'as he advised them') · also los de 'those of' (con los de Castejón 'with the men of Castejón')
fijos: fijo — son (masc. pl.; fijos dalgo 'sons of something', noblemen; = hijos) · also fijos — children, sons and daughters together (los yernos e las fijas todos vuestros fijos son)
qué: qué — what a …! (exclamative) · also qué — what? which? (interrogative pronoun/adjective, as in de qué será pagado, 'with what will he be satisfied') · indirect: que non sabe qué se far '(so that) she knows not what to do'; avemos qué fablar 'we have something to speak of' · also qué — how (exclamative before an adverb: qué bien pago 'how well he paid')
fonta: fonta — outrage, affront; harm (Pidal: 'ultraje, afrenta', and 'daño' in general; tóvoslo a grand fonta 'he took it as a great affront'; non temién ninguna fonta 'they feared no harm'; = afrenta, ultraje)
mio: mio — my (unstressed possessive; mio Çid 'my lord Cid')
darvos: dar + vos — to give you (infinitive + enclitic vos)
he: aver — I have (1st sg. present; perfect auxiliary, = he, and the auxiliary of the split future, e.g. doblar vos he) · also he — and (a spelling of e; he de fijas de mio Çid 'and of the daughters of my Çid')
algo: algo — something; the poem's discreet word for money, wealth · also algo — somewhat, something (algo vidie 'he saw something', i.e. something of what pleased him); que él preçiava algo, 'which he prized not a little' (sense uncertain)
villas: villa — town (fem. pl.; ganar aquellas villas 'to take those towns'; = villas)
dar: dar — to give (infinitive; split future dar gelos [hemos] = se los daremos) · also dar salto 'to make a dash, sally' (salto davan); dar çevada 'to give barley, feed the horses' · also dar — to give way, yield (oviéronse a dar 'they had to give way'; = ceder, rendirse)
axuvar: axuvar — trousseau, the bride's household goods (Arabic; adúzenvos axuvar 'they bring you the trousseau', Pidal 'os traen el ajuar para el casamiento'; = ajuar)
marcos: marco — mark (a unit of weight for silver, pl.)
palafrés: palafré — palfrey, riding horse (pl.; a gentle horse for ordinary riding rather than war; = palafrenes)
gruessos: gruesso — big, sturdy, heavy-built (masc. pl.; cavallos gruessos 'strong, stout horses'; = gruesos)
sazón: sazón — due season, prime condition; de sazón 'in good condition, fit' (palafré de sazón 'a palfrey in prime condition', probably; = sazón)
diestro: diestro — right (hand, side), noun use (de diestro 'on the right'; = diestro, closest derecha) · also diestro — adjective 'right' (so diestro braço 'his right arm'); mio diestro braço 'my right arm', figuratively my chief support · also en diestro — led unmounted at the rider's right hand, of the warhorse (buen cavallo en diestro 'a good warhorse led at his right'; Pidal: cavallo en diestro, Old French destrier)
corredores: corredor — raider, outrider sent out to scour the country (masc. pl.; davan sus corredores 'he sent out his raiders'; = corredores, closest 'exploradores, incursores') · also corredor — swift, fast-running (adjective, of horses; cavallos gruessos e corredores 'stout, swift horses'; = veloces)
muchas: mucho — many (fem. pl.; muchas son las arrobdas 'many are the watches'; = muchas)
dos: dos — two · also do + se, 'when/where … (they)' (Dos fallan con los moros 'when they come upon the Moors', Pidal 'cuando se encuentran'; = cuando se encuentran) · also do + se, 'where … (he might)' with a subjunctive (non vido … dos alçasse 'he saw nowhere he might hide', Pidal 'donde se escondiese')
colada: Colada — Colada, a sword, won by the Çid at Tévar (hi gañó a Colada 'there he won Colada'; = Colada)
tizón: Tizón — Tizón, the sword of King Búcar, won by the Cid (proper name; = Tizón)
bien: bien — well · bien — good, benefit (noun; algún bien vos pueda far 'some good I may do you') · bien — very, quite, intensifying an adverb (bien çerca del agua 'very near the water')
sabedes: saber — you know (present 2nd pl., old -edes ending; = sabéis)
guisa: guisa — manner, fashion; a guisa de 'in the fashion of' · a vuestra guisa 'as you see fit, in your own way' (prended a vuestra guisa 'take as you please') · also de guisa que 'in such a way that' (de guisa irán por ellas que … 'in such a manner will they go for them that …'; = de modo que) · also a fea guisa 'in a shameful fashion' (sácanlos de las huertas mucho a fea guisa 'they drive them out most shamefully')
varón: varón — man, male, man of worth (= varón)
sodes: seer — you are (2nd pl. present, used respectfully to one person; = sois; old -edes ending, cf. odredes, vedes, catedes)
me: me — me, to me · also reflexive 'myself' (fata que yo me pague 'until I am satisfied')
coraçón: coraçón — heart (= corazón) · also por coraçón 'willingly, heartily, with a will' (lo an por coraçón) · also de coraçón 'heartily, with a will' (adóbanse de coraçón 'they arm with a will')
sepan: saber — may know, should know (present subjunctive 3rd pl.)
riqueza: riqueza — wealth, riches (fem. sg.; D'aquesta riqueza 'of this wealth'; = riqueza)
sirvades: servir — you serve, may serve (present subjunctive 2nd pl., old -ades; cómmo las sirvades 'how you are to serve them'; = sirváis)
si: si — if; si + subjunctive alone = 'if only …!' · si non — otherwise, if not (si non, do sopiéredes 'if not, wherever you learn'); si + future subjunctive 'if' (si nos falláredes 'if you find us') · also si — si'nulla = sin + nulla with -n assimilated before n- (si'nulla dubda 'without any fear' (or 'doubt'); = sin ningún miedo, sin ninguna duda) · also si non — 'except, but for' (si non a estos cavalleros 'except these knights'; = salvo) · also si — 'so', optative, = sí, with the present subjunctive in an adjuration (si vos vala el Criador 'so may the Creator help you')
han: aver — they have (present 3rd pl.; = han); after an infinitive, the auxiliary of a split future (seervos han = os serán) · also han a + inf. 'they have to, are bound to' (mandado de so señor todo lo han a far); 'they hold, possess' (que moros las han) · also perfect auxiliary 'have' with a participle agreeing with its object (la ganançia que han fecha 'the booty they have made')
iffantes: infante — child, young child (pl., spelt with ff; = niños); also a young man of noble birth · also iffantes — the infantes of Carrión, young noblemen, sons of a noble house (estos iffantes amos 'these two infantes'; = infantes)
conpieçan: conpeçar — they begin (present 3rd pl.; conpieçan la razón 'they begin the talk'; = comienzan, empiezan)
mandó: mandar — he ordered (preterite 3rd sg.; = mandó) · also mandar — 'he held, governed' a place (Çorita mandó 'he held Çorita'; el que mandó a Mont Mayor 'he who governed Mont Mayor')
pagados: pagar — paid, satisfied (past part. masc. pl.; todos sodes pagados 'you are all satisfied'; = pagados)
todo: todo — all, every (de todo conducho, 'with every kind of provision') · also todo — adverbial 'wholly, all over' before an adjective (todo suzio 'all filthy')
so: so/su — his, her, its (unstressed possessive sg.; so çervicio = su servicio); also seer — I am (1st sg. present; = soy; so ayrado, 'I am in [the king's] ira') · lo so — 'what is his, his own' (neuter article + possessive; lo so puede menguar 'what is his may dwindle') · also so — their (so consejo 'their counsel', so vino 'their wine'; = su)
ya: ya — O! (vocative particle, Arabic yā); also 'now, already' · also ya — 'would', reduced imperfect of aver as conditional ending, 3rd sg., after infinitive + clitic (pagar se ya 'would be satisfied'; = -ía)
cargar: cargar — to load; al cargar de las arcas, 'at the loading of the chests'
nuevas: nueva — news, tidings (fem. pl.; sus nuevas legavan 'his news was arriving'; = noticias, nuevas) · also nuevas — renown, fame (las nuevas de mio Çid sonando van; Pidal 'renombre, fama') · also nuevas — affairs, doings (las nuevas del cavallero 'the knight's affairs'; Pidal 'los asuntos, los negocios') · also nuevas — exploits, deeds (las nuevas que faze el Campeador; Pidal 'las hazañas que hace')
mayor: mayor — larger, greater (aquella mayor az 'that greatest line'; = mayor) · also Mayor — part of the place name Mont Mayor, Montemayor (the Portuguese town, Pidal) · also la mayor — 'the great', standing epithet of Valencia (Valençia la mayor)
prenden: prender — they take, seize (present 3rd pl.; = prenden)
armas: arma — weapon, arms (pl.; armas de lidiar 'weapons for fighting'; en armas 'in arms, armed'; = armas) · also armas — men-at-arms, armed men (treynta mill de armas 'thirty thousand armed men') · also armas — armour, defensive gear (nol falssan las armas 'they do not pierce his armour'); armas de señal 'arms with a device' (see señal)
cavalgan: cavalgar — they ride, mount (present 3rd pl.; = cabalgan)
vigor: vigor — vigour, force; a vigor 'swiftly' (Pidal 'con presteza'; cavalgan a vigor 'they ride swiftly'; = con presteza)
quieren: querer — they wish, are about to (present 3rd pl.) · also querer — they love, hold dear (que vos quieren sin hart 'who love you without guile')
amas: amos — both (fem. pl., Latin ambas; las manos amas 'both hands'; = ambas)
don: don — don, lord (honorific title) · also don — gift (noun; en don 'as a gift') · also don — from where, whence (= donde, de onde; Castejón don abremos grand enpara 'Castejón, from which we shall have great protection') · 'whereof, with which' (Pidal 'de lo cual'; don yo sea pagado 'whereof I may be satisfied') · also don — when, where (= donde, of time; Don llegan los otros 'when the others come up')
elvira: Elvira — Elvira, one of the Cid's two daughters (doña Elvira, also printed don Elvira; = Elvira)
sol: sol — sun · also 'even, so much as' (sol non 'not even'; sol non será penssado 'it will not even be thought of') · also sol — so + l, 'under the' (so 'under', Latin sub, + el before a vowel): del sol espada 'from under the sword' (the likeliest reading; the construction is uncertain) · also Sol — doña Sol, one of the Cid's two daughters (personal name) · also sol — so + el, 'under the' (metiós sol esçaño 'he got under the bench'; here the sense is clear)
fincaron: fincar — they planted, pitched (preterite 3rd pl.; fincaron las tiendas 'they pitched the tents'; = hincaron, plantaron)
inojos: inojo — knee (= hinojo; fincar los inojos 'to kneel')
antel: ante + el — before the (preposition ante + article el; = ante el)
merçed: merçed — mercy, favor; Merçed! 'have mercy, I beg you' (= merced) · also merçed — grace, favour (con la merçed del Criador 'by the grace of the Creator') · also en vuestra merçed 'at your disposal, at your command' (en vuestra merçed somos nos; Pidal 'estamos a vuestro mandar')
padre: padre — father · el Padre santo, God the Father
delant: delant — ahead, in front (apocopated adverb; = delante) · also delant — before, in front of (preposition; Parávas delant al Campeador 'he took his stand before the Campeador'; = delante de)
debdo: debdo — debt, obligation (= deuda); aver en debdo 'to be bound by a vow'
es: seer — it is (present 3rd sg.) · also ser as perfect auxiliary of intransitives (exido es 'has gone out') and passive auxiliary (la tienda es cogida) · also es — that (apocopated esse = ese, demonstrative; en es alcaz 'in that pursuit', por es logar 'through that place')
ayades: aver — you may have (present subjunctive 2nd pl., old -des ending; = hayáis)
vuestros: vuestro — your (masc. pl.; = vuestros) · also los vuestros — 'your men' (possessive with article as a noun; vos con los vuestros 'you with your men')
menssajes: menssaje — message, or the messenger who carries it (masc. pl.; enbió sos menssajes 'sent his messages'; = mensajes, mensajeros)
elle: elle — he (old form of él, Latin ille; elle fizo = él hizo; Pidal restores el[le])
avedes: aver — you have (2nd pl. present, -edes; perfect auxiliary with a participle, me avedes mandado 'you have granted me'; = habéis)
id: ir — go! (2nd pl. imperative; id vos 'go (you)', with reflexive vos; = id, idos)
commo: commo — as, like (spelling variant of como) · how, that, in the way that (commo sirva a doña Ximena 'how he is to serve doña Ximena'); like (commo la uña de la carne) · also commo si + imperfect subjunctive — 'as if' (commo si escapasse 'as if he were fleeing') · commo que 'as one who' (commo que ira a de rey … es echado 'as one who has the king's anger and is cast out') · also commo — 'as soon as, when' (commo gelo a dicho 'as soon as he told it him'); 'since, as' (commo fío por Dios 'as I trust in God')
tengo: tener — I hold (present 1st sg.; en grado vos lo tengo 'I hold it to you in thanks', I am grateful; = tengo) · also tener que — 'I think that' (tengo que vos avrá pro 'I think he will be of use to you'; = creo que)
casadas: casar — married, settled in marriage (past part. fem. pl.; tener por casadas 'to count themselves married'; = casadas)
manos: mano — hand (pl.); dar las manos = the handclasp that makes an agreement binding · a las manos 'for the hands' (pidió agua a las manos 'asked for water to wash his hands'); bolver las manos 'to ply the hands', busy eating · also a las manos tomar 'to take by the hand' (a las manos les tomó, Pidal 'los tomó de la mano')
besavan: besar — they were kissing (imperfect 3rd pl.; las manos le besavan 'they kissed his hands'; = besaban)
su: su — his, her, its · also su — their (aquella su almofalla 'that host of theirs')
guarnimientos: guarnimiento — clothing and finery, attire (pl.; Pidal: 'vestidos y aderezo de una persona'; de los mejores guarnimientos 'with the finest attire'; = atavíos)
salien: salir — they were leaving, came out (imperfect 3rd pl. in -ién; Salien de Valençia 'they were leaving Valencia'; = salían)
ifantes: infante — young nobleman, son of a noble house (pl., spelt Ifantes; = infantes)
espidiéndos: espedir + se — taking leave (gerund espidiendo + enclitic se, its e lost; espidiéndos de Roy Díaz 'taking leave of Roy Díaz'; = despidiéndose)
sues: su — his, her (fem. pl. possessive, old sue/sues; = sus)
compañas: compaña — company, band of troops (pl.; = compañas, closest tropas) · also compaña — the people of one's house, kin and household (de sus compañas, aquellas que avien dexado 'of their people, those they had left behind')
huerta: huerta — irrigated garden land, orchard-plain (fem.; miran la huerta 'they look on the huerta'; = huerta)
teniendo: tener — holding (gerund; teniendo a la çaga 'holding the rearguard'; = teniendo)
va: ir — he/she goes (present 3rd sg.; = va); ir + gerund, 'to be (gradually) doing' · ir + infinitive 'goes to' (la manol va besar 'goes to kiss his hand', el Duero va passar 'goes to cross the Duero') · also va — 'there is, goes on' impersonal (¡Qué priessa va en los moros! 'what a stir there is among the Moors!')
víolo: veer + lo — vio 'he saw' (preterite 3rd sg.) + lo 'it, him' (object pronoun split out; = lo vio)
buena: bueno — good (fem.); en buen(a) '(born/girded) in a good hour' — the poem's honorific formula
cinxo: çeñir — he girded (strong preterite 3rd sg., Latin cinxit; en buen ora cinxo espada 'in a good hour he girded on the sword'; = ciñó)
serién: seer — they would be (conditional 3rd pl., imperfect-type ending -ién; = serían)
sin: sin — without · also sin — 'besides, apart from' (sin las peonadas 'besides the foot-soldiers'); sin falla 'without fail'; sin dubda
ha: aver — he has (3rd sg. present; = ha) · ha — to (a with h-, aver a + inf. 'will, must': lo an todos ha far 'all are to do it'); aver — has, possesses (las fijas que ha 'the daughters she has') · also ha — future ending after infinitive + clitics, the split future (tornar nos la ha 'he will give it back to us'; = nos la tornará) · also ha — there is, there are (impersonal; dos señas ha cabdales 'there are two chief banners'; = hay) · also ha — perfect auxiliary 'has' before the participle (ha vendido 'has sold'; fechos los ha ricos 'has made them rich') · also 'has, gets' (de señor non ha graçia 'he has no favor from a lord') · also ha de + inf. 'is to' (que los ha de aguardar 'who is to attend them'; aver de + infinitive, = ha de) · also non ha qui + inf. — 'there is no one to' (impersonal ha 'there is'; non ha qui tomallos 'there is no one to take them'; = no hay quien) · also ha — of time elapsed, 'it is, it has been' (Pocos días ha … que 'it is a few days since'; = hace)
